proposals.after: He rose to honorary Grand Commandant and was made Prince of Shanggu.

The name 朱延壽 is Zhu Yanshou; 'Yanzhou' is a recurring misspelling.

proposals.before: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says he came from Shucheng in Luzhou.)〉
proposals.after: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says Yanshou came from Shucheng in Luzhou.)〉
proposals.reason: The Chinese explicitly names 延壽, so restoring Yanshou also removes the local name omission.

proposals.after: Early in Tianyou, Yang Xingmi dominated the Huai-Hai region; Yun held Xuancheng and Yanshou held Shou prefecture.

proposals.before: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says that early in Tianfu, with the court driven west, Zhaozong heard of Yanzhou's ability and sent Li Yan secretly to name him Cai commissioner.)〉
proposals.after: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says that early in Tianfu, with the court driven west, Zhaozong heard of Yanshou's ability and sent Li Yan secretly to name him Cai commissioner.)〉
proposals.reason: Both instances of 延壽 refer to Zhu Yanshou, not Yanzhou.

proposals.before: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals》 says Xingmi sent Tai Meng and Wang Maozhang by land while Yun fought at Guangde, was routed, and fled to Wanyang with survivors.
proposals.after: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals》 says Xingmi sent Tai Meng and Wang Maozhang by land; Yun entrusted the fleet to Wang Jian and Wang Tan, then fought at Guangde, was routed, and fled to Wanyang with survivors.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic translation omits 汪建 and 王壇 and their command of Tian Yun's fleet.

proposals.before: At the start of Guanghua, Kuangning because the Founder had the Qingkou defeat secretly attached to the Huai barbarians; the Founder sent Clan Uncle Cong with troops to attack him.
proposals.after: At the start of Guanghua, because the Founder had been defeated at Qingkou, Kuangning secretly attached himself to the Huai forces; the Founder sent Shi Shucong with troops to attack him.
proposals.reason: 氏叔琮 is the personal name Shi Shucong, not the kinship phrase 'Clan Uncle Cong'.

proposals.before: (The 《New Tang History》 says he died in Tianfu 1; Yanwei seized power until Yiangong, with Zhao Kuangning, ousted him.)〉
proposals.after: (The New Tang History says: Man died in Tianfu 1; his son Yanwei established himself; Yanwei's younger brother Yiangong joined Loyalty and Righteousness military commissioner Zhao Kuangning to drive out Yanwei.)
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English retains Chinese book-title brackets and a trailing Chinese close-bracket, and compresses the succession so that 'until Yiangong' obscures that Yanwei seized power and Yiangong later ousted him with Zhao Kuangning.

proposals.before: Barbarian serpents, crafty and cunning, deeply had the father's manner; burning ruins and villages, rowing boats and oars, up and down between Nanjun and Wuchang—nearly no people.
proposals.after: A crafty southern barbarian, deeply having his father's manner: burning ruins and villages, plying boats and oars, up and down between Nanjun and Wuchang—nearly no people remained.
proposals.reason: 蠻蜒 is an ethnonym for southern tribal peoples, not 'serpents'; the literal rendering invents a wrong sense and leaves the subject grammatically plural against the singular successor in context.

proposals.before: The Founder issued an edict Hunan military commissioner Ma Yin and Jingnan military commissioner Gao Jichang to drill elite troops five thousand, send general Ni Kefu to command them, descend on Li prefecture, and unite with Tan troops.
proposals.after: The Founder issued an edict ordering Hunan military commissioner Ma Yin and Jingnan military commissioner Gao Jichang to drill five thousand elite troops, send general Ni Kefu to command them, descend on Li prefecture, and unite with the Tan troops.
proposals.reason: Literal English omits the verb governing the commissioners after 'edict', producing an ungrammatical clause that obscures who was ordered.

decisions.reason: s0021 has 檢校太尉; 太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand General, and the proposed idiomatic otherwise preserves the rise to office and the Shanggu princely enfeoffment.
s0086 names 朱延壽; Yanshou is the correct reading, and Yanzhou is an unsupported misspelling.
The note explicitly opens with 延壽 as the subject of the native-place statement; restoring Yanshou matches the Chinese and removes the pronoun omission without changing the Shucheng-in-Luzhou fact.
s0089 has 延壽為壽州刺史; the office-holder is Zhu Yanshou, so replacing Yanzhou with Yanshou corrects the name while leaving the Tianyou, Yang Xingmi, and Tian Yun material intact.
s0095 has 時延壽方守壽春; the defender is Yanshou, not Yanzhou, and the proposed clause is otherwise accurate.
s0097 twice names 延壽 (闻延壽有武幹…授延壽蔡州節度使); correcting Yanzhou to Yanshou restores the right person without altering Zhaozong, Li Yan, or the Cai appointment.

decisions.reason: s0108 states 頵委舟師於汪建、王壇 before Yun's Guangde battle; the before text omits that fleet entrustment, and the proposed idiomatic restores Wang Jian and Wang Tan accurately.
s0152 has 遣氏叔琮率師伐之; 氏叔琮 is the personal name Shi Shucong, not a kinship phrase 'Clan Uncle Cong', and the rewritten literal keeps the Guanghua, Qingkou, and Huai attachment facts.

s0221 has 子彥威自立，弟彥恭結忠義節度使趙匡凝以逐彥威; the before compression 'until Yiangong' invents a wrong succession sequence, while the proposed idiomatic restores Yanwei's self-establishment and Yiangong's later expulsion with Zhao Kuangning.
